title: VIRMS Architecture Phase 1 — Platform Core + Authentication Foundation
status: PROPOSED FOR REVIEW; explicit implementation approval and affected decision gates remain required
objective: Extend the existing Django modular monolith into a secure PostgreSQL-backed Company/Branch account and authorization foundation. Reuse existing identity and Tenant models; implement no business modules in Phase 1.
authorization: This operation writes only these two requested plan artifacts. No application code, dependency, database, credential, frontend, canonical document or handoff change is authorized.
No commit, push, merge, pull, branch switch, deployment or production/staging mutation. Preserve all pre-existing dirty work.
Implementation is a separate approval. A plan approval cannot resolve a BUSINESS DECISION REQUIRED by implication. No Phase 2 planning.

accounts.User extends AbstractBaseUser/PermissionsMixin, UUID PK, unique login_id/email, active/staff/first-password flags and creator/updater references. AUTH_USER_MODEL=accounts.User, USERNAME_FIELD=login_id, REQUIRED_FIELDS=[email]. UserManager accepts manually supplied login_id.

Tenant has UUID, name, unique slug, is_active. TenantMembership has User/Tenant/assigned_by, effective interval, PROTECT FKs, valid-interval check and one-open-row partial uniqueness. Reuse Tenant as Company; labels/slug are attributes, not identity.
RoleAssignment is global User/role/effective interval with no Company FK. can_manage combines global role with membership. This is incomplete V2 Company-specific authority.

Current active_roles/active_tenant_ids/can_manage accept only effective_until=NULL. Finite future expiry currently denies access, not ordinary half-open interval semantics. This difference must not be silently migrated.

Session/CSRF login, logout, me, current-password change, temporary provisioning/reset and account status exist. Selected commands use atomic transactions and locks; password change validates a stale User before acquiring any User lock.

AccountSecurityEvent covers successful account actions, required actor/subject, action, tenant_ids, outcome. It is not yet a general append-only administrative audit. LoginAttempt stores HMAC Login-ID failure state and progressive cooldown.

Admin registers User, RoleAssignment, Tenant and TenantMembership. Admin deletes denied, but raw save/password/privilege and queryset/widget paths require audit and scope review. First-password middleware currently applies only to /api/.
No Branch, BranchAssignment, Company-scoped grant, module-state model, revoke-all command or health/readiness endpoints in inspected backend. No business-module backend implemented.

accounts and tenants each have local 0001_initial migration. README warns starter migrations were replaced. Applied database ledger/schema/rows unknown; never rewrite or assume these migrations are unapplied.

official_sources.finding: 5.1 absent from supported series; propose supported Django 5.2 LTS secure patch, reverified and exactly pinned at implementation.
Keep existing custom User/AUTH_USER_MODEL; adapt custom admin forms and authorization boundary.
Password hash changes invalidate other sessions; update_session_auth_hash preserves current self-change session. Epoch is a proposed project extension, not a built-in feature.
Unsafe cookie requests require CSRF. Anonymous login needs separate unconditional CSRF protection.
Built-in cache throttles permit concurrent races; strict shared admission needs its own atomic implementation.
Use explicit command atomic boundaries; account for rollback and failure audit outside aborted transaction.
FK/check/unique constraints enforce row integrity; cross-table Company equality cannot be implemented as ordinary CHECK. Use narrowly scoped consistency triggers where needed.

inferences_proposals: Reuse apps.accounts/apps.tenants/apps.common/core. Retain internal Tenant naming and /tenants URLs; Company is its business meaning, not another table.

CompanyRoleGrant belongs to membership, with optional Branch. NULL Branch represents an explicit Company-wide grant, never inferred from no assignments. Existing global back_office remains platform role source; legacy global business roles cease to authorize after reviewed cutover.
Extend AccountSecurityEvent as the single administrative/security audit source, not a competing audit ledger.

No persisted business module configuration in Phase 1: typed module hook, unsupported/unknown module default deny, core operations separately registered. No financial permissions or OFF exceptions invented.

Proposed technical security defaults for approval: minimum password length 12, accept long passphrases, no composition regex; session absolute lifetime 12 hours, idle timeout 30 minutes, configurable shorter Admin sessions. Exact retention/source/global rate budgets require measured operator security configuration before release. These are proposals, not canonical business rules.

architecture_diagram:
flowchart TD
  C[Browser or operational Admin] --> H[Session + CSRF + request ID + account/epoch]
  H --> V[Validated API or Admin command input]
  V --> P[Live Company membership + scoped role + Branch + module + object/field policy]
  P --> Q[Scoped read selectors]
  P --> W[Command: lock + reauthorize + mutate + audit atomically]
  Q --> DB[(Single PostgreSQL authority)]
  W --> DB
  W --> E[AccountSecurityEvent]
  E --> DB
  DB --> R[Allowlisted response; bounded scoped cache later]
  R --> C

app_boundaries.owns: Environment/settings, root routing, session/epoch enforcement, default-deny DRF wiring, request/probe wiring. Client-selected Company is only an untrusted selector.

Existing User, global platform-role source, scoped CompanyRoleGrant, credential/session lifecycle, limiter, authorization policy, AccountSecurityEvent and account commands. Add services/selectors/policy modules only when needed.
Existing Company/Tenant, membership, Branch/BranchAssignment, scoped selectors and administrative commands. Retain package exports and model layout.
Existing UUID base plus small safe request-ID/error/metadata helpers. No business modules, generic repositories, event bus or permission DSL.
Existing private S3-compatible adapter retained; no upload/media endpoint or provider change.

identity_authentication.identity: Keep UUID User, unique login_id/email and existing manager. Do not change login normalization, case uniqueness or email requirement without a decision. No generated human Login ID.
identity_authentication.bootstrap: After approved isolated migrations/rehearsal: python manage.py createsuperuser --email mullas313@gmail.com; operator supplies login_id and password interactively. No execution now, no password fixture/migration/source/shell argument. Existing create_superuser sets must_change_password=False for private interactive bootstrap. Validate password through supported command/admin validators. Superuser is break-glass system identity, not an automatic Company business grant.
flows: CSRF GET → login POST → rotated backend session → minimal me. First-login session only csrf/me/logout/password change; same gate for Admin deep links and password paths.

Own change: lock fresh User, validate current password/status/epoch, new confirmation/validators/new!=current; commit hash/flag/epoch/audit atomically, preserve only current session with refreshed hash/epoch.

Provision: authorize approved Company/Branch/role, atomically create User/grants/audit, generate temporary credential in memory, persist hash only and deliver once to authorized initiator in no-store response over secure transport. No credential retrieval API or response-body logging.

Reset: verify business identity by controlled operator procedure, require safe reason, lock target and reauthorize global lifecycle permission; rotate credential/epoch, require private replacement, invalidate old sessions.
Deactivate: global authority under BDR-03, inactive/unusable credential/epoch bump, preserve grants/history. Reactivation alone cannot restore old sessions/credential; fresh reset required.
Compromise revoke: explicit authorized reasoned command increments epoch without mandatory password mutation; next protected request rejects prior sessions.
identity_authentication.hashing: Use supported Django PBKDF2 and current cost defaults after framework upgrade, retain old-hash upgrade compatibility. Common/similarity/minimum validators; no predictable composition rules. set_password alone does not validate: services/Admin/API must validate. Never reveal permanent plaintext/hash.
identity_authentication.session_login_race: Login and self-change must not stamp a fresh epoch onto a stale authenticated User. Verify credentials/activity/epoch against locked fresh User; concurrent reset/revoke/deactivate serialized before session issuance. A session from old credentials cannot inherit new epoch.
identity_authentication.security_policy_gate: Accept proposed expiry/minimum length and operator temporary-delivery/retention policy during plan review. No new email/phone verification or public recovery flow.

company_branch_authorization.company: Reuse Tenant UUID/name/slug/is_active; inactive means operational suspension, no delete/merge. Normal activity denies; specifically authorized Platform recovery/activation uses separate audited control-plane policy, never private-finance wildcard access.
company_branch_authorization.membership: Effective interval proposed [from, until), null means open. Active User/Company additionally required. Close/append rows, immutable user/company/start. Existing finite-future rows require BDR-01 explicit mapping because current code denies them. Phase1 writes do not create scheduled/future-ending rows; existing finite history retained without granting it implicitly.
company_branch_authorization.roles: CompanyRoleGrant membership + role(owner/accountant/investor/media) + nullable Branch + interval + assigned_by. Company-wide grant explicit. Branch-local action needs both effective grant and effective BranchAssignment in same membership/Company. Global back_office only platform capability; Company access separately scoped. Legacy global non-platform rows preserved for trace, never fallback authorization after cutover.
company_branch_authorization.branches: UUID, immutable Tenant PROTECT FK, name and timestamps. No Branch-name identity/uniqueness/coded limit/default Branch. Inactive lifecycle only after BDR-04; identity and assignment foundation can proceed without inactive actions.
company_branch_authorization.assignments: BranchAssignment membership/Branch PROTECT FKs, actor and interval. Same-Company enforced for assignment AND scoped role grant in services and PostgreSQL triggers. Cannot reparent Branch/membership or grant foreign Company access.
company_branch_authorization.temporal_integrity: Effective access is intersection of current User/Company, membership interval, role-grant interval and (for Branch-local action) BranchAssignment interval. Persisted child intervals may outlive a closed parent; they are ineffective and cannot attach to a replacement membership UUID. Ending parent does not rewrite or auto-reopen child history. New grants/assignments must start no earlier than membership and are created now/open; future starts/ends and unsupported overlaps rejected in Phase1 administrative writes under stable parent locks. Legacy finite/overlap rows require approved mapping before any reinterpretation. Do not claim full stored interval containment or an exclusion constraint that has not been implemented.
company_branch_authorization.policy: authorize(actor, action, company, branch=None, resource=None, fields=None): live account/epoch/password gate → current Company membership → explicit action/role grant → Branch assignment/scope → module hook → object ownership/Company/Branch → field allowlist. Scope queryset before object lookup. Client Company/Branch IDs are not authority. No first-membership selection.
phase1_matrix: Self me/logout/password: authenticated self and first-login allowlist.

Company summary: preserve current allowed role cases only with explicit scoped grants; do not add Investor Company-directory visibility. Branch summary limited to granted operational metadata.
No financial/Investor/Media business operation registered; unknown module/action denies.
company_branch_authorization.platform_admin: Django groups/user_permissions/is_superuser/is_staff do not confer business action authority. Bootstrap break-glass can establish approved initial platform grants by reviewed operator procedure; normal APIs still require scoped policy. No self-service privilege elevation.
company_branch_authorization.module_hook: Typed core operation registry plus optional module identifier/operation class. No persistent business-module-state implementation. Unsupported module denies; future provider distinguishes ordinary writes, authorized history and separately approved open-obligation actions, never wildcard OFF bypass.
company_branch_authorization.history: No consolidation, reparent or historical financial rewrite. Same-Company previous-Branch business-history rules remain a future resource-selector obligation, not permission to read every Branch today.
company_branch_authorization.platform_scope_representation: No new platform grant entity: active global RoleAssignment(role=back_office) represents platform identity; explicit current TenantMembership represents authorized Company control-plane scope, combined with the approved core action matrix. CompanyRoleGrant covers only business roles and cannot confer platform powers. This global platform-role plus explicit membership rule is intentional for control-plane administration, not the forbidden legacy global BUSINESS-role Cartesian mapping. Company-specific provisioning/Branch/membership actions require both. company.create and bootstrap establishment are explicitly Company-less platform actions under approved platform action policy; creation never silently grants membership. Initial membership/platform role comes from explicit approved operator bootstrap manifest. Suspension recovery requires current effective explicit Company membership and current platform role plus approved recovery action, ignoring only Company.is_active; historical/ended membership alone never authorizes recovery. No private-data wildcard access. BDR-02 gates matrix/delegation entries.

concurrency_transaction_idempotency.linearization: Sensitive write acquires current actor/target User and scope parent locks, then rechecks credentials/session epoch/current membership/grant/Company state inside transaction. Revocation/suspension/grant end uses the same locks. If revoke wins first, write denies; if an authorized write commits first, revoke applies afterward. Middleware checks alone do not cancel in-flight writes.
concurrency_transaction_idempotency.lock_order: Proposed global order: User UUIDs sorted, Company UUIDs sorted, TenantMembership UUIDs sorted, Branch UUIDs sorted, grant/assignment UUIDs sorted. All account/Admin/Company/grant mutations must follow this order, including new insert paths. Lock stable parents, not only existing child rows; short transactions, no external delivery under lock.
concurrency_transaction_idempotency.atomicity: Command state and success audit commit together; integrity failure handled after rollback. Denial/failure event written separately, sanitized, without accidentally committing partial mutation.
concurrency_transaction_idempotency.retry: Status desired-state and end operations are idempotent no-ops after reauthorization, no duplicate state-change success event. Provision/reset/password change are unsafe to automatically retry. On unknown response inspect authorized state, then deliberately issue a new audited reset if temporary delivery was lost. No plaintext replay storage or generic idempotency platform in Phase1.

coverage: Protected Admin actions and denied/failed outcomes
audit_architecture.write: Success state/audit atomic; failure/denial audit after rollback in bounded separate transaction. Audit failure makes sensitive mutation fail closed. Denial audit failure never authorizes the action. No dummy User for Company events.
audit_architecture.append_only: Application/Admin no update/delete; runtime DB role SELECT/INSERT only on event table, no UPDATE/DELETE/TRUNCATE. Separate migration-owner role, guard triggers for accidental ORM/bulk changes. DB owner can still tamper; do not claim WORM/tamper-proof.
audit_architecture.visibility: Control-plane global account events are operator-only by default. Company reviewers see only explicitly Company-scoped event projections; mixed-Company tenant_ids/before-after data never serialized wholesale. No authorization from JSON tenant_ids. Branch audit reads also scope filtered.
audit_architecture.privacy: Allowlist actor/resource UUID, UTC time, action/outcome/reason, request ID and minimum safe old/new. Never password/hash/temp credential/session/CSRF token/secret or raw body/object dump. Review Admin LogEntry repr/change message and APM capture. Retention and support access require accepted operator policy, not invented business visibility.

api_foundation.request_analysis: No observed request trace proves REDUNDANT/DUPLICATE; no removal/merge justified. Inventory actual demos/other callers before compatibility change.

new_calls.contract: Scoped paginated id/tenant_id/name summaries; allowlisted name search/order, stable UUID tie-breaker.
Authorized same-Company Branch summary or hidden 404.
Explicit authorized reasoned compromise revoke; detail response, BDR global authority.
Process existence only; no DB/secret disclosure.
200 only when bounded DB check and required migration graph applied; otherwise generic 503. Never migrate in probe.

api_foundation.errors: Add error.code/message/fields/request_id retaining existing detail/errors fields for compatibility. Normalize Django JSON, DRF, middleware, CSRF, API 404/405 and unexpected failures. 400 invalid input, 401 invalid session, 403 CSRF/first-password/known forbidden, 404 hidden object, 409 duplicate/version conflict, 429 bounded Retry-After, 503 unavailable dependency, 500 generic failure. No traceback/DB/credential/identifier existence leak.
api_foundation.reads: Default 20 retained; proposed maximum 100 on new lists, no unbounded list-all. Scope first, allowlist search/filter/sort, stable id tie-break. Explicit serializers, no all-fields/public internal schema.
api_foundation.commands: Thin input adapters → current policy → atomic service → state/audit → committed response. No GET/startup mutation; no generic Company/account CRUD. API/Admin use same command authority. Unknown outcome is not safe automatic retry.
api_foundation.context: Company/Branch path/body is selector; conflicting parent/object IDs deny. Selected Company in session is UX hint only. context revision derived from live grants, not client permission token.

threats: Login hash-work exhaustion and temporary-response leakage
controls: CSRF required for anonymous login and all unsafe cookie requests/Admin. HttpOnly session; Secure outside loopback local HTTP; SameSite Lax with same-origin/same-site topology. No localStorage token authority.
No wildcard credentialed CORS or CSRF disabling. Prefer same-origin future API routing; cross-site hosting topology requires separate review.

Shared PostgreSQL limiter reserves admission before password hashing; identifier plus trusted source/global budgets, bounded body, progressive cooldown, no worker sleeping or permanent lockout. Apply to Admin login too.

Keep current 3-failure backoff up to 300 seconds as initial compatibility baseline; source/global limits selected from measured hashing cost and expected usage before release. HMAC source identifiers, bounded expiry cleanup command, no Redis/Celery needed.

Request IDs generated/validated with bounded characters/length, returned as X-Request-ID. Structured logs safe actor/scope/error code only; disable body/token/credential capture in logs/APM/Admin messages.
Transactions reauthorize under stable parent locks; handle integrity errors after rollback and return safe conflicts, never false success.
security_environment.configuration: Retain DJANGO_ENV local/staging/production, explicit allowed hosts, DEBUG local only, loopback development HTTP, private local .env and controlled injected secrets elsewhere. DATABASE_URL precedence documented; PostgreSQL only. Tests explicitly isolated DB/role, never shared data.
security_environment.tls_proxy: Non-local secure cookies/redirect/HSTS require verified trusted HTTPS proxy that sanitizes forwarding headers; source IP cannot be trusted from arbitrary X-Forwarded-For. Explicit CSRF origins; hosting provider/domain remain configurable.
security_environment.versions: Upgrade proposed to supported Django 5.2 LTS secure patch and compatible supported DRF; resolve exact pins at implementation with official release notes/compatibility checks. Exact runtime/container patch/digest and transitive lock. No unrelated bulk upgrade.
security_environment.packaging: Reuse current PostgreSQL devcontainer/volume, no second DB technology or down -v. Verify collectstatic hashed manifest for actual non-local storage and non-root startup, without real secrets or DB connection at build. No automatic migration.
security_environment.future_ops: Production separately requires accepted RPO/RTO, backups/tested restore, limited runtime versus migration DB roles, TLS/secret injection, Admin exposure and incident revoke procedures. No deployment here. Session expiry, retention and rate technical settings require accepted operator policy.

local_first_compatibility.authority: Django + PostgreSQL alone commit authoritative truth. Same Django APIs for later web/local clients. No client financial posting authority.
local_first_compatibility.reads: Bounded authorized recent cache can filter/search/sort locally; growing datasets use server pagination/filter/search/sort. Manual/controlled refresh and future TanStack Query, no full growing database fetch or polling added now.
local_first_compatibility.cache_scope: Future keys include User UUID, Company UUID, Branch scope, operation/filter/page and context revision. Clear on logout/account/Company switch/session 401/scope change; revalidate before protected activity. Server rejects stale authority independently.
local_first_compatibility.versions: Opaque live context revision supports invalidation; entity updated_at/revision supports later conditional reads. This is not a sync protocol and cannot remotely delete offline copies.
local_first_compatibility.privacy_gate: Persistent private-data caching/offline retention/encryption needs later approval. No SQLite, packaging, queue, drafts/sync/conflict engine implemented in Phase1.

migration_sequence: M0: identify approved local/test DB/roles/version and inspect ledger/schema/row counts/starter history read-only. Stop on ambiguity. No fake-initial/reset/drop/flush/replacement initial migrations.
M1: additive successor User epoch/audit/limiter fields, nullable historical scope. Preserve old event values/IDs; unknown stays unknown, never guessed.

M2: tenants Branch then BranchAssignment; accounts CompanyRoleGrant depends on TenantMembership/Branch. Successor cross-app dependencies avoid circular initial migrations. Exact filenames assigned from actual graph, not fabricated here.

M3: checks/partial uniques and named PostgreSQL same-Company/ownership/audit guard triggers plus separate runtime privileges. Validate existing intervals/data before stricter enforcement. No unreviewed extensions.

M4: approved mapping manifest for actual User/membership/role/Branch rows; no Cartesian role×membership or default Branch. Legacy finite-future and overlap rows require explicit treatment. Empty verified database needs no historical backfill. Bounded repeat-safe historical-model backfill only for explicit mappings.

M5: reader cutover after reviewed mapping; scoped API/Admin policy replaces global business-role helpers, legacy records retained. Revoke pre-cutover sessions. Expansion → mapping → readers → enforcement; no partially mixed authorization rollout.

M6: disposable PostgreSQL fresh replay and representative old-foundation upgrade, UUID/history/count/constraint/trigger/privilege checks, measured timings and restore/forward-fix evidence. Reverse additive schema only before dependent new data exists.
